properties.description: --http <addr> serves the design over streamable HTTP so many client sessions share one process. The store is single-writer PER PROCESS, so this satisfies the constraint rather than working around it: one server means exactly one writer. rmcp builds a service per session through a factory, and ReflowService::share decides the split — the graph and the write generation are shared because they are properties of the design; the seat and the read-hint memory are minted fresh because they are properties of whoever just connected. The graph moved from a Mutex to an RwLock so concurrent reads do not queue behind each other, and the compiler audited the read/write split in the process: all 32 read sites genuinely need only &DesignGraph. No authentication — the flag's help and the startup line both say to bind loopback or a private network.
properties.name: Several sessions work one design at once, through one server
